definition: A treatment facility is a clinical setting where people receive care or therapy. In this context, it refers to a service site that may be specialized, such as a trauma center, or non-specialized.

reasons: The packet does not provide a general definition of “treatment facility” (e.g., as a clinical setting where people receive care/therapy).
The packet only mentions “specialized trauma centers” and feasibility in a “non-specialized treatment facility,” without stating what a treatment facility is or its broader meaning.
Claims in the definition about “trauma center” as an example and “specialized, such as…” are not explicitly defined or supported as the term’s meaning in the packet.

The packet only supports the term in the narrow sense of a specialized or non-specialized treatment site; it does not define a treatment facility as any clinical setting where people receive care or therapy.
The added gloss “or therapy” is unsupported by the source text.
The definition goes beyond the packet’s wording by generalizing from ‘specialized trauma centers’ and a ‘non-specialized treatment facility’ to a broader service-site definition.
